record.paper_title: Grothendieck’s inequality and completely correlation preserving functions - a summary of recent results and an indication of related research problems
record.original_question: Develop mathematical objects that play the role of “non-commutative copulas” and “non-commutative distribution functions” for modeling non-commutative dependence in quantum theory, in a setting where entanglement, Bell-type phenomena, and Tsirelson-type bounds are linked to the real Grothendieck constant.

evidence.quote: Even a mathematical modelling of non-commutative dependence in quantum theory and its applications to quantum information and quantum computation is strongly linked with the existence of the real Grothendieck constant K R G.
Keeping a non-commutative version of Grothendieck’s inequality at the back of our mind (cf. [33, 38, 39]) these facts might lead to problems of the following type:
(3-RP1) Look for objects like “non-commutative copulas”, leading to a search for “non- commutative distribution functions”.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A (classical) bivariate copula is a function $C:[0,1]^2\to[0,1]$ satisfying $C(u,0)=C(0,v)=0$, $C(u,1)=u$, $C(1,v)=v$, and the 2-increasing condition $C(u_2,v_2)-C(u_1,v_2)-C(u_2,v_1)+C(u_1,v_1)\ge 0$ for all $u_1\le u_2$, $v_1\le v_2$ in $[0,1]$. By Sklar's theorem, every joint cumulative distribution function $H$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ with marginals $F,G$ admits a representation $H(x,y)=C(F(x),G(y))$ for a copula $C$, so copulas encode the dependence structure of pairs of real random variables independently of their marginals.

In the quantum/non-commutative setting, pairs of "random variables" are replaced by (possibly non-commuting) self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space, equipped with a state, and the joint distribution function in the classical sense is generally not defined because the spectral projections need not commute. The phenomena of entanglement, Bell-type correlation inequalities, and Tsirelson-type bounds for quantum correlation matrices are quantitatively governed by the real Grothendieck constant $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$, which is the smallest constant such that for every $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$, every real matrix $(a_{ij})$, and all unit vectors $x_i,y_j$ in a real Hilbert space,
$$\Big|\sum_{i,j} a_{ij}\,\langle x_i,y_j\rangle\Big| \;\le\; K_G^{\mathbb{R}}\;\sup\Big\{\Big|\sum_{i,j} a_{ij}\,s_i t_j\Big|:\; s_i,t_j\in\{-1,+1\}\Big\}.$$

Problem. Construct a class of mathematical objects, to be called "non-commutative copulas," together with an associated notion of "non-commutative (joint) distribution function," such that:

(i) The class reduces to the usual class of bivariate copulas (and to ordinary joint cumulative distribution functions) when restricted to pairs of commuting self-adjoint operators with a common spectral resolution.

(ii) There is an analogue of Sklar's theorem: every admissible non-commutative joint object factors through a non-commutative copula and the (one-variable) spectral distributions of its marginals.

(iii) The class supports a "non-commutative dependence" theory in which entanglement, Bell-type correlations, and Tsirelson-type quantum-correlation bounds for pairs of self-adjoint contractions on Hilbert space arise as natural functionals, with extremal/limiting quantities expressible in terms of the real Grothendieck constant $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$.

Give precise definitions of these objects, prove the analogue of Sklar's theorem in this setting, and exhibit the link to $K_G^{\mathbb{R}}$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for "non-commutative copulas" in connection with Grothendieck's inequality and quantum dependence returns no developed theory; it is posed as a research program rather than a settled construction. No publications were found that define non-commutative copulas with an associated Sklar-type theorem and a link to the real Grothendieck constant, so the problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Some points of view on Grothendieck's inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing Grothendieck's inequality, completely correlation preserving functions, and links to quantum correlation bounds; lists related research directions.
status_evidence.claim: Non-commutative analogues of copulas are mentioned only as a direction for future research, not as an established theory.

status_evidence.title: Tight Hardness of the Non-Commutative Grothendieck Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the non-commutative Grothendieck inequality from a complexity-theoretic angle without addressing copulas or Sklar-type decompositions.
status_evidence.claim: No notion of non-commutative copula or non-commutative distribution function is developed in this line of work.
